name: rooted_nae_cycle_fibre_An
statement: For n >= 4, indices in Z/nZ: A_n = {(a,b_1,...,b_n) in {+-1}^{n+1} : a+b_i+b_{i+1} in {+-1} for every i}. On the half a=1 the condition excludes exactly the local pattern b_i=b_{i+1}=1, so S={i : b_i=1} is an independent (stable) set of the cycle C_n and every independent set occurs; the half a=-1 is its antipode. a is the 'root'/homogenizer coordinate.
notes: This single family is the object of S10-S14. n >= 4 is used so that the cliques of C_n are exactly the empty set, the vertices and the edges.

name: dgeo_dcb_for_this_source_range
statement: d_geo(A) = minimum dimension of a real residual subspace R inducing no more signed projective classes on the full dual than the ambient rank r permits (a 'feasible geometric quotient' has at most r signed classes, counting one zero class if it occurs). d_cb(A) = minimum, over coordinate bases drawn from the full dual together with signed selectors, of dim of the common residual space. Every selector certificate is in particular a feasible geometric quotient, hence d_geo(A) <= d_cb(A) always.
notes: Anchor definition for the whole S10-S14 range; d_geo <= d_cb is the direction used to turn the mod-2 lower bound into a lower bound on d_cb.

name: rooted_nae_cycle_full_dual_Dn
statement: The projective full dual of A_n is exactly D_n = {A, B_i, C_i : i in Z/nZ} with A=e_0, B_i=e_i, C_i=e_0+e_i+e_{i+1}. Proof: normalize a sign-valued affine form on the positive half to value -1 at the empty independent set; its values on the singletons force every singleton increment to be 0 or 2, so the form is -1+2|S cap K| for a vertex set K; it is sign-valued on every independent set iff K is a clique; for n>=4 the cliques of C_n are the empty clique, the vertices and the edges. The edge forms cut out the defining condition, so the fibre is FULL CLOSED. Rank r = n+1 (witnessed by the empty and the n singleton independent sets).
source: dossier p.158 (S10 lines 102-131, (11)-(13); r=n+1 at line 99)
notes: Full closure matters: the counterexample family is not a nonspanning or non-closed artefact. Repeated verbatim at S12 (3) p.174 and S14 (5) p.185.

name: rooted_nae_cycle_cardinality_and_defect
statement: |A_n| = 2*I(C_n) = 2*(F_{n-1}+F_{n+1}) = 2*L_n (L_n the n-th Lucas number); rank r = n+1; density defect ell(A_n) = n - log_2 L_n. Explicit Lucas values used: (L_4,...,L_13) = (7,11,18,29,47,76,123,199,322,521); L_42 = 599074578. For even n, L_n = phi^n + phi^{-n} > phi^n, so ell(A_n) < n(1 - log_2 phi).
notes: L_42 = 599074578 re-derived independently by this digester from the Lucas recurrence: MATCHES. ell(A_42) = 42 - log_2(599074578) = 12.8418396275, matching S11's printed digits exactly.

name: cycle_two_shadow_quotient_lemma_2_1
statement: (Lemma 2.1, cycle two-shadow quotient.) Let S_n = {0} u {u_i : 1<=i<=n} u {u_i+u_{i+1} : 1<=i<=n} in F_2^n, u_i the standard basis, indices cyclic. For EVERY subspace W <= F_2^n of dimension w, the number of occupied cosets obeys |S_n/W| >= 2n+1-3w. Proof: pick Q subset [n], |Q|=n-w, whose singleton cosets are a basis of F_2^n/W; deleting the w vertices of [n]\Q from a cycle destroys at most 2w edges, so at least max{0,n-2w} edges have both endpoints in Q; their images are sums of two distinct basis vectors, mutually distinct and distinct from 0 and every singleton. Count 1+(n-w)+max{0,n-2w}; for w<=n/2 this is the bound, for w>=n/2 the first two terms already are.
notes: The coefficient 3 is EXACT: quotienting by <u_i> identifies the three pairs 0~u_i, u_{i-1}~u_{i-1}+u_i, u_{i+1}~u_i+u_{i+1}, and widely separated choices of i make the bound an equality (S10 (19), p.160). This is the whole source of the n/3 rate and of 'one residual direction pays three quotient mergers'.

name: saturated_lattice_mod2_transfer
statement: Transfer from real signed projective classes to a binary quotient. Given a real residual R of dim d, replace R by R_0 = span of (every f in D_n in the zero class) and (every f - sigma*g in R, sigma in {+-1}, witnessing a class equality). R_0 is rational, contained in R, of dim d_0 <= d, and induces exactly the same classes. Put Lambda = R_0 cap Z^{n+1}; it is saturated, hence a direct summand of Z^{n+1}, so its mod-2 reduction has dimension d_0. Signs die in characteristic two, so the real signed partition (zero class included) REFINES the coset partition mod Lambda-bar. All D_n vectors have odd weight; translating by A=e_0 lands in the even-weight space E with basis u_i=e_0+e_i, sending A->0, B_i->u_i, C_i->u_i+u_{i+1}. Set W = Lambda-bar cap E, dim W <= d_0 <= d.
source: dossier pp.160-161 (S10 lines 199-256, (20)-(24)), audited at pp.167-169 (S11 lines 30-107)
notes: No reduction-of-rank assumption is hidden: passing to the SATURATED lattice is precisely what stops a denominator divisible by 2 from invalidating the mod-2 argument (S10 lines 269-272, p.162). The zero class costs no lost +1 (S11 lines 104-106). Field-critical: the argument is R -> F_2 and uses sigma=+-1 |-> 1.

name: primitive_lattice_dimension_preservation
statement: (S11 audit of the transfer.) Lambda = R_0 cap Z^{n+1} is primitive: if k*z in Lambda with z in Z^{n+1}, k != 0, then k*z in R_0, hence z in R_0, so z in Lambda. Equivalently Z^{n+1}/Lambda is torsion-free and Lambda extends to an integer basis, so dim_{F_2} Lambda-bar = d_0 exactly. Consequently k_{D_n}(R_old) >= |S_n/W| >= 2n+1-3*dim W >= 2n+1-3d.
notes: This is the audit's fully-justified version of the chain; the audit's only requested change is to write d_0 <= d explicitly rather than silently reuse d.

name: signed_class_lower_bound_corollary_3_1
statement: (Corollary 3.1, eq (25).) For every real residual space R of dimension d, the number k_{D_n}(R) of signed projective classes on D_n (counting one zero class if it occurs) satisfies k_{D_n}(R) >= 2n+1-3d.
notes: Uniform in n, no computational input. This is the only lower-bound engine in the whole S10-S14 range.

name: dgeo_rooted_nae_cycle_exact
statement: (S10 eq (2).) For every n >= 4, d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3). Lower bound: a feasible geometric quotient has at most r = n+1 signed classes, so Corollary 3.1 forces n+1 >= 2n+1-3d, i.e. d >= ceil(n/3). Upper bound: choose an independent U in V(C_n) with |U| = ceil(n/3) and take R = span{L_u = A+B_u : u in U}; modulo R, adding or deleting a vertex of U from a clique does not change its signed class, so classes are indexed by cliques of C_n - U, which has n-|U| vertices, n-2|U| edges and no clique bigger than an edge: at most 1+(n-|U|)+(n-2|U|) = 2n+1-3|U| <= n+1 classes.
notes: Uniform in n with NO computational input (earlier support had been exact finite searches only). Independently re-verified here by exhaustive search over all residual spaces of dim <= ceil(n/3)-1 spanned by zero-class forms and signed differences, n=4..8: zero feasible quotients (see local_rerun_exhaustive_dgeo_minimality).

name: dcb_geq_dgeo_rooted_nae_cycle
statement: (S10 eq (30).) Since every selector certificate is in particular a feasible geometric quotient, d_cb(A_n) >= d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3).
notes: Matching upper bound d_cb <= ceil(n/3) is supplied independently by S12 and S14, closing d_cb = d_geo.

name: rooted_nae_full_dual_matroid_three_connected
statement: (Lemma 5.1.) For every n >= 4 the real projective matroid on D_n is three-connected. Proof: the n fundamental relations C_i - A - B_i - B_{i+1} = 0 give a dual representation (up to column signs) by t = sum_i e_i, p_i = e_i, q_i = e_i+e_{i+1} in R^n, of rank n. No loops, coloops or singleton one-separations. For a partition (X,Y) with |X|,|Y| >= 2 and t in X, set a = #{i : p_i in X}, b = #{i : q_i in X}; a case analysis on the pinned forest components of the X- and Y-edge systems gives (n-r(X))+(n-r(Y)) <= n-2, i.e. lambda(X) = r(X)+r(Y)-n >= 2. Duality preserves the connectivity function.
notes: This is what makes the counterexample fatal to the three-connected shortcut: the obstruction is NOT produced by a hidden 1- or 2-separation. [EXTRACTION-UNCERTAIN, harmless] the extraction prints 'qquad' without its backslash inside (32) and (34); spacing only, no mathematical content lost.

name: three_connectivity_endpoint_cases_b0_bn_over_R
statement: (S11 audit sec.3, the two endpoint cases done over the REALS.) With delta_X = n-r(X), delta_Y = n-r(Y), t in X: (b=0) if a<n then delta_X = n-a-1 and, since |X|>=2 gives a>=1 while the Y-system holds the full cycle plus at least one Y-pin so delta_Y = 0, the sum is <= n-2; if a=n then delta_X=0 and the unpinned full Y-cycle has defect 0 for odd n and 1 for even n. (b=n) if a=0 then delta_Y=0 and the full X-cycle has defect 0 for odd n, while for EVEN n its alternating null vector survives the total-sum equation so delta_X=1; if a>0 an X-pin kills the cycle nullspace so delta_X=0 and delta_Y=a <= n-2 by |Y|>=2.
notes: FIELD-SENSITIVE: the even-cycle alternating null vector is real and must not be discarded; the audit flags exactly this. S10's own text compresses these cases ('the full Y-cycle is killed by any Y-pin; with no pin it has dimension at most one'), which the audit expands.

name: singleton_connectivity_lambda_one
statement: (S11 audit completion.) Every displayed dual column is nonzero; deleting t or any q_i leaves all p_i and hence full rank; deleting p_i leaves p_j (j != i) together with q_i = p_i+p_{i+1}, so also full rank. Therefore every singleton has lambda({e}) = 1+n-n = 1, not zero. Combined with lambda(X) >= 2 for |X|,|Y| >= 2 this proves genuine 3-connectivity, including the smallest endpoint n=4.
notes: One of the two clarifications the audit asks to be made explicit; it changes no stated bound.

name: ceiling_rado_constant_one_claim
statement: DISPROVED. The three-connected strengthening 'q_ev(A) >= floor(log_2|A|), and hence d_cb(A) <= ceil(ell(A))' (S10 eq (1)) is FALSE, even for an infinite family of full-closed fibres whose projective full-dual matroids are genuinely three-connected. The rooted NAE cycles are the counterexamples.
source: dossier p.156 (S10 lines 5-14), verdict audited PASS at p.173 (S11 lines 303-309)
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: three-connectivity plus full closure are NOT enough to force constant one; the failure is extensive (deficit n/3+O(1) against defect (1-log_2 phi)n+o(1)), not a finite anomaly.

name: q_ev_floor_log_cardinality_rado_claim
statement: DISPROVED. By the Rado certificate lemma, a bound q_ev >= floor(log_2|A_n|) would imply the contradicted ceiling bound; therefore q_ev(A_n) < floor(log_2|A_n|) (S10 eq (41)) for every member of the subfamily n = 0 mod 6, n >= 42, DESPITE Lemma 5.1 (three-connectivity).
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: a maximal evaluation-row Rado argument cannot have the hoped-for constant one on three-connected blocks. The dossier does not restate the Rado certificate lemma itself in pp.156-200 (UNKNOWN in this range).

name: three_connected_block_ceiling_charging_shortcut
statement: DISPROVED (S10 sec.7). The proposed global shortcut -- 'decompose the full dual into three-connected matroid blocks, and charge every three-connected block with the ceiling estimate d_cb <= ceil(ell)' -- is ruled out: the rooted NAE cycles are ALREADY single three-connected blocks and the failure is extensive rather than an isolated finite anomaly (exact geometric deficit n/3+O(1) against density defect (1-log_2 phi)n+o(1)).
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: block decomposition into three-connected pieces gives no entropy payment. A block decomposition proof needs a genuine entropy loss INSIDE a three-connected cyclic block; it cannot declare every such block ceiling-rigid (S10 lines 64-67, p.157).

name: infinite_ceiling_counterexample_family
statement: For even n, L_n = phi^n + phi^{-n} > phi^n, hence ell(A_n) = n - log_2 L_n < n(1-log_2 phi). With delta = 1/3 - (1-log_2 phi) = 0.0275752469..., if n = 0 mod 6 and n >= 42 then delta*n > 1, so ell(A_n) < n/3 - 1 and ceil(ell(A_n)) <= n/3 - 1 < n/3 = d_geo(A_n) <= d_cb(A_n). Hence (S10 eq (5)) d_cb(A_n) >= n/3 > ceil(ell(A_n)) for every such n.
source: dossier pp.165-166 (S10 lines 420-451), audited p.173 (S11 lines 266-301)
notes: First member n=42: L_42 = 599074578, ell(A_42) = 12.8418396275..., d_geo(A_42) = 14; delta*42 = 1.15816037248... > 1. All four numbers independently re-derived here and matching (delta*42 agrees to 10 of the 11 printed digits; last digit is rounding).

name: n13_ceiling_counterexample
statement: Exact finite counterexample at n=13: d_cb(A_13) >= d_geo(A_13) = 5 while L_13 = 521 and ell(A_13) = 13 - log_2 521 = 3.9748604377..., so ceil(ell(A_13)) = 4 < 5. Audit's explicit certificate: U = {1,3,5,8,11} (one-based cyclic) is independent of size five; C_13 - U has 8 vertices and 3 edges so the certificate has at most 1+8+3 = 12 <= 14 = r classes; conversely a residual space of dimension four would have at least 2*13+1-3*4 = 15 > 14 classes.
notes: Re-verified here: gaps of U are 2,2,3,3,3 (sum 13, all >= 2 so independent); C_13-U = {2,4,6,7,9,10,12,13} with edges 6-7, 9-10, 12-13, exactly 3. This is a FINITE certificate about n=13, not an asymptotic claim.

name: dgeo_over_ell_ratio_limit
statement: (S10 eq (6).) d_geo(A_n)/ell(A_n) -> 1/(3(1-log_2 phi)) = 1.090186..., phi = (1+sqrt5)/2. Consequently the rooted NAE cycles do NOT disprove an absolute linear theorem d_cb = O(ell); what they show is that neither three-connectivity nor a maximal evaluation-row Rado argument can have the previously hoped-for constant one.
notes: Re-derived here as 1.090186485. CAUTION for downstream use: this 1.09 is the ROOTED-NAE-CYCLE family's ratio only; it is NOT the campaign's constant floor. Within pp.156-200 the largest forced constant is C_int = 2.949539... (S14, intervals uniform over descendant attachments).

name: entropy_payment_inside_a_three_connected_cyclic_block
statement: S10 sec.7's statement of what remains: one residual direction can account for THREE quotient mergers in this family (exactly as in the tightness example (19) of Lemma 2.1), and those directions must be paid at positive entropy cost throughout the cyclic block. Merely invoking three-connectivity or maximal Rado transversality cannot supply that payment. The family remains compatible with a constant-factor conditional-counting or activation theorem, so it is NOT a counterexample to the desired global O(ell) conclusion.
notes: This is what S12/S14 then supply FOR THIS FAMILY (activation cells). It is exactly the piece that remains unsupplied for dense connector-incoherent cores -- the campaign's single hardest open piece.

name: s11_audit_verdict_pass_two_clarifications
statement: Independent audit of rigidity_attack_report.md: VERDICT PASS. The main theorem d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3) (n>=4) is correct, the full-dual real matroid is three-connected, the n=13 example is a valid ceiling counterexample, and every n = 0 mod 6, n >= 42 belongs to the asserted infinite family. No substantive gap was found in the mod-2 transfer, the upper certificate, or the endpoint connectivity cases. Two sentences should be made explicit: (1) after rationalizing the residual space, denote its dimension d_0 <= d rather than silently reusing d; (2) after proving lambda(X) >= 2 for |X|,|Y| >= 2, separately note that every displayed dual column is a nonloop and noncoloop, disposing of singleton one-separations. Neither point changes any stated bound.
source: dossier p.167 (S11 lines 3-27), final assessment p.173 (S11 lines 303-309)
notes: NOT independent evidence in the campaign's sense: S11 audits S10 by reading it. It IS an independent re-derivation of the endpoint connectivity cases and of the n=13 arithmetic.

name: independent_dominating_set_gap_table_all_residues
statement: For every n >= 4 an independent set U of C_n of size ceil(n/3) exists with all cyclic gaps of length 2 or 3: n = 3k -> |U| = k, gaps 3,...,3; n = 3k+1 -> |U| = k+1, gaps 2,2,3,...,3; n = 3k+2 -> |U| = k+1, gaps 2,3,...,3. The residuals L_u = A+B_u = e_0+e_u are linearly independent because the e_u coordinate occurs only in L_u. With F_empty = -A, F_{i} = B_i, F_{i,i+1} = C_i one has F_{u} - F_empty = L_u and F_{u,v} - F_{v} = L_u, so every clique form is congruent mod span{L_u} to the form obtained by deleting its U-vertices. Deleting an independent U removes exactly 2|U| cycle edges.
source: dossier pp.169-170 (S11 lines 110-166), same table at p.175 (S12 eq (5), lines 63-72)
notes: Proves feasibility in ALL THREE congruence classes mod 3, not only 3 | n. All gaps >= 2 (independence) AND <= 3 (domination) are both load-bearing -- see coverage_check_enforces_dominating_gaps.

name: dcb_equals_dgeo_rooted_nae_cycle
statement: (S12 eq (1).) For the rooted NAE cycle fibre, for every n >= 4: d_cb(A_n) = d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3). The geometric lower bound of S10 is ATTAINED by an actual coordinate-basis selector certificate, so the family is a solved high-corank cyclic class.
source: dossier p.174 (S12 lines 16-18), independently re-proved with a different basis at p.184/p.189 (S14 (1),(21))
notes: Two DIFFERENT explicit bases prove the upper bound (S12 sec.3 and S14 (14)); see s12_and_s14_selector_bases_differ.

name: explicit_selector_basis_gapwise_S12
statement: Selector basis (S12 sec.3). Orient the cycle; for a length-two gap u-v-u' select B_v, C_v; for a length-three gap u-v-w-u' select B_v, C_v, C_w. Let B_U = {A} together with all gap-selected forms; every gap of length g contributes g forms so |B_U| = 1 + sum_gaps g = n+1 = r. Independence: in a putative dependence the coordinate B_{u'} occurs in exactly one selected form of the preceding gap (its final C-form), so that coefficient vanishes; moving backwards through the gap kills the rest, then A. Representatives modulo R = span{L_u}: A and the selected forms represent themselves; B_u = -A for u in U; in a length-three gap B_w = C_w (C_w-B_w = L_{u'}); the edge form leaving u in U obeys C_u = B_v (C_u-B_v = L_u). These cases exhaust D_n, so d_cb(A_n) <= dim R = ceil(n/3).
notes: Explains the three-at-a-time quotient mergers of the binary lower bound: a length-three gap is paid by ONE residual direction while retaining a genuine coordinate-basis transversal. This is the basis implemented by the S13 checker.

name: gap_factorization_f2_f3
statement: (S12 (12)-(13).) Once the states at U are prescribed, independent-set choices factor over the gaps. For a length-two gap with endpoint states s,t in {0,1}: f_2(s,t) = 2 if s=t=0, else 1; and f_2(s,t) <= 2^{1-(s+t)/2}. For a length-three gap (its two interior vertices form an edge): f_3(s,t) = 3 if s+t=0, 2 if s+t=1, 1 if s+t=2; and f_3(s,t) <= 2^{2-(s+t)/2}.
notes: Both exponent bounds are tight only at their extreme states (f_2 at s=t=0 and at s+t=2). Multiplying over the cyclic gaps works because each selected u is an endpoint exactly TWICE, so sum of (s+t)/2 over gaps = |z|, and sum of (g-1) over gaps = n-d.

name: activation_cell_inequality_cycle_S12
statement: (S12 eq (2)/(14).) For u in U put Z_u = 1{L_u != 0}; on the half a=1 this is 1{u in S} for the corresponding independent set S, and the half a=-1 is antipodal with the same activation vector. Then for every z in {0,1}^U the number of independent sets with S cap U = z is at most 2^{n-d-|z|}, and restoring the antipodal half gives |A_{n,z}| <= 2^{n+1-d-|z|} = 2^{r-d-|z|}, with r = n+1 and d = ceil(n/3).
notes: This is the UNCONDITIONAL (root-marginal) form. S14 (24) upgrades it to a TARGET-UNIFORM form conditional on an arbitrary incoming boundary value w -- that stronger version is the one the connector programme needs.

name: aggregate_three_quarters_power_density
statement: (S12 eq (15).) Summing the activation-cell bound over z gives |A_n|/2^{n+1} <= (3/4)^d, hence d <= ell(A_n)/log_2(4/3). The exact Lucas-number density is stronger asymptotically, but (15) is the TENSOR-STABLE bound needed by the activation programme.
notes: 1/log_2(4/3) = 2.409420840... . Measured here: the bound is LOOSE by a factor 2-5 against the exact Lucas density (n=16: L_n/2^n = 0.0337 vs (3/4)^6 = 0.1780). So it never pins d; see activation_cell_bound_is_not_tight_on_the_cycle.

name: connector_transversality_root_boundary_S12
statement: (S12 sec.5.) Treat A = e_0 as the incoming boundary coordinate and the B_i = e_i as private. Projection of R = span{L_u} to the private space sends L_u |-> B_u and is injective, hence R cap span{A} = {0} (eq (16)). Thus the selector space creates NO new boundary-only residual direction and the connector-absorption clause holds for every ancestor residual space. Conditioning on the root sign leaves a uniform independent-set fibre, so L_{B|A} = n - H(B|A) = n - log_2 L_n = ell(A_n) (eq (17)). Together with (15) this is a conditional linear certificate with constant 1/log_2(4/3) and NO connector surcharge.
notes: The constant here (2.4094) is better than S14's cycle constant 2, but it is the ROOT-CONDITIONED statement; S14 (2) proves the stronger target-uniform version over an arbitrary junction basis W containing A.

name: entropy_weighted_short_gap_witness_generalization
statement: (S12 sec.6, scope.) The construction solves a genuine infinite family of three-connected, high-corank cyclic blocks. It does NOT prove the universal linear theorem: the key extra structure is the independent dominating set whose short gaps simultaneously provide (1) one residual direction per three cycle vertices, (2) a full-dual coordinate transversal, and (3) a product activation profile. The remaining global problem is to replace these short-gap witnesses by an entropy-weighted analogue in an ARBITRARY singleton-layer cyclic block.
notes: The three ingredients are separable and are enforced by DIFFERENT checks: (2) by coordinate-basis coverage, (3) by the activation matching. Measured here that (3) alone does not pin the dimension -- so the hard transfer is of ingredients (1)+(2), not of the counting profile.

name: exact_rational_selector_checker_S13
statement: Checker using ONLY integer arithmetic and fractions.Fraction (no floating point). construction(n) builds A = e_0, B_i, C_i, the residuals {A+B_u : u in starts} and the S12 gap-wise basis. structural_check(n) asserts: |starts| = d = (n+2)//3; gaps in {2,3}; |basis| = r = n+1 and rank(basis) = r; |residuals| = d and rank(residuals) = d; and that EVERY form of D_n is 'covered', i.e. there is a basis element b and a sign in {-1,+1} with rank(residuals + [form - sign*b]) = d (the selector residual lies in R). activation_check(n) enumerates all independent sets of C_n, groups them by z = restriction to starts, and asserts count <= 2^{n-d-|z|} and 2*count <= 2^{n+1-d-|z|}. Defaults: structural n = 4..30, activation n = 4..16.
notes: The checker verifies the SPECIFIC construction; it does NOT minimize over all bases/selectors, so it cannot by itself certify that d_cb equals ceil(n/3) rather than merely being at most it. The lower bound is entirely S10's mod-2 argument.

name: s13_checker_rerun_counts
statement: Local re-run of the S13 checker at its default ranges: STRUCTURAL PASS n = 4..30; ACTIVATION PASS n = 4..16; endpoint independent_sets = 2207, largest_cell = 324 at n = 16. Per-n (n, total independent sets, largest cell, d): (4,7,4,2) (5,11,6,2) (6,18,9,2) (7,29,12,3) (8,47,18,3) (9,76,27,3) (10,123,36,4) (11,199,54,4) (12,322,81,4) (13,521,108,5) (14,843,162,5) (15,1364,243,5) (16,2207,324,6). The totals equal L_n exactly for every n in the window, confirming |A_n| = 2*L_n.
source: dossier pp.180-183 (S13 lines 1-146) -- counts computed by this digester, not printed in pp.156-200
notes: PROVENANCE: the dossier reproduces the checker SOURCE but not its printed output anywhere in pp.156-200, so these counts are this digester's re-run (Python 3.14.3, exact Fraction arithmetic, 2026-08-19), NOT a dossier quotation. Evidence about the finite windows n <= 30 / n <= 16 only. Observed pattern (not proved): for n = 3k the largest cell is 3^k.

name: s14_enumeration_22_is_not_the_s13_checker
statement: S14 eq (22) reports 'exact basis-and-selector enumeration for 4 <= n <= 8' giving d_cb = 2,2,2,3,3. The S13 checker reproduced at pp.180-183 does NOT perform that enumeration: it verifies one fixed construction. The code behind (22) is not reproduced anywhere in dossier pp.156-200.
source: dossier p.189 (S14 lines 228-239) vs pp.180-183 (S13 lines 1-146)
notes: UNKNOWN whether the (22) enumeration code survives anywhere. This digester supplied an independent exhaustive minimality search instead (local_rerun_exhaustive_dgeo_minimality, n = 4..8) which reaches the same values by a different route.

name: s14_cycle_selector_basis_eq14
statement: (S14 (10)-(20).) Put d = ceil(n/3), s = 3d-n in {0,1,2}; choose cyclically ordered U = {u_1,...,u_d} with exactly s gaps of length two and d-s of length three (lengths sum 2s+3(d-s) = n). Write a length-two gap as u_j,m_j,u_{j+1} and a length-three gap as u_j,m_j,w_j,u_{j+1}. Then B_n = {A} u {C_{u_j,m_j} : all j} u (length-three gaps) {C_{m_j,w_j}, B_{w_j}} u (length-two gaps) {B_{m_j}} has 1+d+2(d-s)+s = n+1 forms and is a coordinate basis: relative to A a length-two gap contributes B_{u_j}+B_{m_j}, B_{m_j}, a length-three gap B_{u_j}+B_{m_j}, B_{m_j}+B_{w_j}, B_{w_j}, on disjoint coordinate sets. Selectors: B_{u_j} -> -A (residual L_{u_j}); B_{m_j} -> C_{u_j,m_j} in a length-three gap (residual -L_{u_j}); with v_j = m_j or w_j, C_{v_j,u_{j+1}} -> B_{v_j} (residual L_{u_{j+1}}).
notes: All selector residuals lie in the d-dimensional R = span{L_u}, so d_cb(A_n) <= d, and with S10's lower bound this proves d_cb = d_geo = ceil(n/3).

name: s12_and_s14_selector_bases_differ
statement: S12 and S14 give two DIFFERENT explicit coordinate bases proving the same upper bound d_cb(A_n) <= ceil(n/3). For a gap starting at u with m = u+1, w = u+2: S12 selects {B_m, C_m} (length two) and {B_m, C_m, C_w} (length three); S14 (14) selects {C_u, B_m} (length two) and {C_u, C_m, B_w} (length three). Both are proved to be coordinate bases drawn from the full dual with all selector residuals in span{L_u : u in U}.
source: dossier pp.175-177 (S12 lines 86-142) vs pp.186-189 (S14 lines 122-221)
notes: Verified by this digester (the S13 code implements S12's basis; S14's differs in which C-form of each gap is taken). Useful downstream: the certificate is NOT unique, so a generalization is not forced to reproduce one particular basis -- only the short-gap structure.

name: dcb_table_n4_to_n8
statement: (S14 eq (22).) Exact basis-and-selector enumeration for 4 <= n <= 8 gives d_cb = 2, 2, 2, 3, 3 for n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 respectively. The dossier states explicitly: 'The computation is only a check; equations (14)-(21) prove all n.'
notes: FINITE WINDOW ONLY (n = 4..8); it is evidence, the proof is (14)-(21). Values agree with ceil(n/3). Independently reproduced here by exhaustive minimality search (see local_rerun_exhaustive_dgeo_minimality).

name: target_uniform_activation_cell_cycle
statement: (S14 (23)-(26).) Z_u = 1{L_u != 0}; after conditioning on the root sign A this is the occupancy indicator of u in the corresponding stable set. Match every u_j to the FIRST vertex m_j of its following gap; the matched vertices are distinct and lie outside U. Fix an activation pattern z contained in U: the d signs on U are fixed and every active u in z forces its matched neighbour to be unoccupied. Hence, FOR EVERY fixed root value and every additional ancestor boundary value w, |(A_n)_{W=w, Z=z}| <= 2^{n-d-|z|}. Incompatible patterns give an empty cell; exactly, on the full rooted cycle the cell count is the number of independent sets of C_n[V \ (U u N(z))]. Summing, |supp(B_1,...,B_n | W=w)| <= 2^n (3/4)^d.
notes: TARGET-UNIFORM is the operative strengthening over S12 (2): the bound holds for every boundary value w, not just on the root marginal. So (14) is not merely a selector basis but a target-uniform CONDITIONAL activation-cell certificate.

name: cycle_connector_absorption_exact
statement: (S14 (27)-(28).) Let W be an incoming junction basis containing A and otherwise disjoint from the private coordinate span Q = {B_1,...,B_n}. Then R cap span W = 0, because a combination sum_u c_u (A+B_u) lying in the boundary has all private coefficients c_u = 0. Therefore for EVERY ancestor residual space R_< contained in span W: R cap span W is contained in R_<, and dim((R+R_<)/R_<) = d = ceil(n/3). This is the exact connector-absorption condition.
notes: Absorption here is FREE (holds for every R_<, even R_< = 0) because the residual space is entirely private. That is exactly what fails for the m=1 interval, where the residuals are entirely BOUNDARY.

name: rooted_connector_estimate_constant_two
statement: (S14 (2), proved via (28)-(34).) If the common root sign A is the incoming boundary and the n cycle signs are private, the residual space has zero intersection with the boundary and its new rank is at most twice the private conditional defect: dim R = ceil(n/3) <= 2(n - H(B_1,...,B_n | W)) = 2 L_{Q|W}. Hence rooted NAE cycles are connector-compatible cyclic SCCs WITH CONSTANT 2, whenever the only shared cycle coordinate is the homogenizing root (additional disjoint ancestor coordinates are harmless). Ingredients: L_{Q|W} >= n - log_2 L_n because every conditional private support sits inside the independent sets of C_n (31); and ceil(n/3) <= 2(n - log_2 L_n) for all n >= 4 (32).
source: dossier p.184 (S14 lines 21-34), proof pp.190-192 (S14 lines 285-367)
notes: Constant 2 for the cycle. Note the completely uniform (weaker-coefficient) version from the activation cells is d <= L_{Q|W}/log_2(4/3), coefficient 2.4094 (S14 (29)-(30), p.191).

name: disjoint_edge_defect_lower_bound
statement: (S14 (33),(33a),(34).) Choosing floor(n/2) disjoint cycle edges and using their NAE constraints gives n - log_2 L_n >= floor(n/2) * log_2(4/3). With beta = log_2(4/3), for n >= 14 one has 2*beta*floor(n/2) >= beta(n-1) >= (n+2)/3 >= ceil(n/3); the middle inequality holds at n = 14 and thereafter the left side has larger slope because beta > 1/3. The ten remaining values 4 <= n <= 13 follow from (L_4,...,L_13) = (7,11,18,29,47,76,123,199,322,521). This proves ceil(n/3) <= 2(n - log_2 L_n) for all n >= 4.
notes: beta = 0.4150375 > 1/3 is the whole slope argument. Re-verified here for 4 <= n <= 200 (no violations), well beyond the proof's own split at n = 14; the ten small cases were checked individually and all hold.

name: path_selector_distance_theorem_4_1
statement: (S14 Theorem 4.1, eq (36).) For the stable-set fibre of the path P_N (full dual D(P_N) = {A} u {B_i : 0<=i<N} u {C_i = A+B_i+B_{i+1} : 0<=i<N-1}, rank N+1, 2N projective forms), for every N >= 3: d_cb(A_{P_N}) = d_geo(A_{P_N}) = ceil((N-1)/3). Lower bound: the same mod-2 translation gives S(P_N) = {0, u_i} u {u_i+u_{i+1}}, and for a w-dimensional quotient kernel the occupied-coset count is at least 1+(N-w)+max{0, N-1-2w} >= 2N-3w; rationalizing and reducing the saturated lattice transfers this to real signed classes; a feasible quotient has at most N+1 classes, so N+1 >= 2N-3w, i.e. w >= ceil((N-1)/3).
notes: The path is the CUT version of the cycle; it is the object that carries the boundary/connector analysis, since its two ends become incoming boundary.

name: interval_selector_basis_table_41
statement: (S14 (40)-(45).) Write N = m+2 with boundary vertices 0, m+1 and private interval 1,...,m; put d_m = ceil((m+1)/3). Choose an independent U in {1,...,m}, |U| = d_m, so every component of P_{m+2} - U has one or two vertices; one fixed choice: m=1 -> {1}; m=2 -> {2}; m=3 -> {1,3}; m=3k (k>=2) -> {2,4} u {7,10,...,3k-2} u {3k} (middle progression empty at k=2); m=3k+1 -> {2,5,...,3k-1} u {3k+1}; m=3k+2 -> {2,5,...,3k+2}. Every two-vertex component {v,w} is immediately followed by a distinct selected u in U; use B_v, C_{v,w}, C_{w,u}; for a one-vertex component {v} use B_v; also use A; finally add B_u for every selected u not occurring in such a block. Take R_m = span{A+B_u : u in U}.
notes: Coordinate-basis proof: relative to A a block is triangular on B_v, B_v+B_w, B_w+B_u and distinct blocks use disjoint selected vertices. Crucially the first and last component representatives are B_0 and B_{m+1}, so {A, B_0, B_{m+1}} is contained in the basis (eq (44)) -- this is what makes the certificate boundary-preserving. Table sizes and independence re-verified here for m = 1..7.

name: boundary_preserving_interval_certificate
statement: (S14 (46)-(48), eq (3).) Regard W = {A, B_0, B_{m+1}} as the incoming boundary and Q = {B_1,...,B_m} as the private junction basis. Eq (44) shows the selector basis preserves every incoming coordinate; since all u in U are private, R_m cap span W = 0. Hence for any previously paid R_< contained in span W: dim((R_m+R_<)/R_<) = d_m = ceil((m+1)/3) and R_m cap span W is contained in R_<. The basis and selectors do NOT depend on the values of the boundary signs, so they survive the genuinely affine conditional fibres created by fixing W.
notes: Boundary-value independence is the property that makes this usable inside a recursive/conditional argument; a certificate that depended on w would not survive conditioning.

name: interval_conditional_entropy_bound
statement: (S14 (49).) For any law supported on the interval constraints, fixing W = w leaves a subset of the independent sets of a path on m vertices. Hence H(Q | W=w) <= log_2 F_{m+2} and L_{Q|W} := m - H(Q|W) >= m - log_2 F_{m+2}.
notes: F_{m+2} is the number of independent sets of P_m. This is the entropy-only route, which is what survives at m = 3 where the sharper cellwise route provably fails.

name: interval_linear_bound_C_int
statement: (S14 eq (4).) For every m >= 2, d_m <= C_int * (m - H(Q|W)) with C_int = 2/(3 - log_2 5) = 2.949539... . Proof: with beta = log_2(4/3), m=2 gives L_{Q|W} >= 2-log_2 3 = beta while d_m = 1; m=3 gives L_{Q|W} >= 3-log_2 5 with d_m = 2, which is EXACTLY the claimed inequality; for m >= 4, floor(m/2) disjoint private edges give L_{Q|W} >= beta*floor(m/2), and C_int*beta > 6/5 follows from (4/3)^5 > (8/5)^3 i.e. 128000 > 124416, so m = 4,5 are immediate and for m >= 6, C_int*beta*floor(m/2) > (6/5)(m-1)/2 = 3(m-1)/5 >= (m+3)/3 >= ceil((m+1)/3).
notes: m = 3 is the tight case (equality by construction), which is why C_int is what it is. The chain 3(m-1)/5 >= (m+3)/3 requires exactly m >= 6, and the integer certificate 128000 > 124416 is exact. All steps re-verified numerically here.

name: C_int_optimality_limit
statement: (S14 (56).) The coefficient C_int = 2/(3-log_2 5) = 2.949539... is OPTIMAL for a theorem uniform over arbitrary descendant attachments. Witness: at m = 3 attach k later stable-set vertices, each adjacent to both boundary endpoints and to no private interval vertex. When both endpoints are unoccupied those later vertices are free and the five private independent sets of P_3 occur with equal multiplicity 2^k; other boundary patterns have only O(1) extensions. As k -> infinity, H(Q|W) -> log_2 5 and d_m/L_{Q|W} -> 2/(3-log_2 5) = C_int.
notes: IMPORTANT FOR THE CAMPAIGN'S CONSTANT FLOOR: within pp.156-200 this 2.9495 is the largest forced constant, exceeding the 1/log_2(4/3) = 2.40942 floor cited from S6 p.113. Any theorem uniform over descendant attachments must tolerate C >= 2.9495 on intervals. Re-derived here numerically: d_m/L -> 2.949539695 (12 digits at k = 40).

name: target_uniform_interval_cells_m2_and_m_ge_4
statement: (S14 (57)-(60).) Except at m = 1 and m = 3, the choice (41) has a matching entirely INSIDE the private interval, u |-> u-1 for u in U. Define Z_u = 1{A+B_u != 0}. For fixed boundary target w and activation pattern z, the d_m private signs on U are fixed and every active u forces its distinct matched private neighbour to be unoccupied, so |Q_{w,z}| <= 2^{m-d_m-|z|} for m = 2 or m >= 4. This is target-uniform in BOTH endpoint signs. Summing gives d_m <= L_{Q|W}/log_2(4/3), coefficient 1/log_2(4/3) < 2.410.
notes: The exception set {1,3} is exactly where u-1 leaves the private interval (U contains 1, so u-1 = 0 is a BOUNDARY vertex) -- verified here against the table (41) for m = 1..7. So the m=1 and m=3 pathologies have the same syntactic cause even though their consequences differ.

name: m3_interval_cellwise_certificate_impossible
statement: (S14 (61)-(62).) At m = 3 the neutral boundary fibre is the five independent sets of P_3. A dimension-two private CELLWISE certificate would imply 5 <= 2^3 (3/4)^2 = 9/2, which is impossible. Concretely, for the residuals U = {1,3} the all-active cell consists of exactly ONE point whereas its putative bound is 2^{3-2-2} = 1/2. Hence the entropy-only estimate, rather than the sharp activation profile, is genuinely necessary for this finite affine interval.
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: m = 3 only. Re-verified exactly here by enumeration: at m = 3 exactly one cell violates (z = (1,1), count 1 > 1/2) and the aggregate 5 <= 4.5 fails; at m = 2,4,5,6,7 there are ZERO violations. This is the falsifier that gives the whole activation machinery teeth.

name: m1_interval_no_absolute_constant_defect_bound
statement: (S14 sec.7, (63)-(64).) The one-private-vertex interval (boundary 0,2, private 1) admits NO defect-only connector bound with an absolute constant. For the neutral boundary state both signs of B_1 occur, so its private defect is zero -- and this can dominate a SPANNING, FULL-CLOSED fibre, not merely an isolated nonspanning boundary state. Attach k further stable-set vertices z_1,...,z_k each adjacent to both boundary vertices 0,2 and to nothing else: in the positive half the neutral endpoint pattern has 2^{k+1} extensions (B_1 and all z_j free), each other endpoint pattern has one. Then H(B_1|A,B_0,B_2) = 2^{k+1}/(2^{k+1}+3) and L_{Q|W} = 3/(2^{k+1}+3) -> 0, while the local path has exact selector distance ONE. So no inequality dim((R+R_<)/R_<) <= C * L_{Q|W} can hold with an absolute C.
notes: THE decisive obstruction in this source range: it is why the connector-absorption clause is a HYPOTHESIS of the open target rather than a convenience. Quantifier detail: the failure is for R_< = 0 (no prepaid boundary residual); with the two boundary residuals prepaid the block is free. Re-derived here exactly for k = 0..7: L = 3/(2^{k+1}+3) matches for every k.

name: m1_exact_absorbed_alternative
statement: (S14 (65)-(67).) The same m=1 block has an exact ABSORBED alternative: use the coordinate basis {A,B_0,B_1,B_2} and assign both edge forms to B_1, giving C_{0,1} - B_1 = A+B_0 and C_{1,2} - B_1 = A+B_2. Both residuals lie entirely in the boundary. If span{A+B_0, A+B_2} is contained in R_<, the block costs ZERO new rank and satisfies connector absorption. If they have not been paid, these residuals violate the absorption condition and one must use the private residual A+B_1, at new cost one. The block is acyclic and belongs in the triangular/ancestor-absorption part of a recursive proof, not in a defect-only cyclic-core theorem.
notes: This is the exact statement behind the campaign's two-regime reading: defect-poor blocks are not uncharted, they have KNOWN zero-cost certificates CONDITIONAL on ancestor payment. The dichotomy (zero new rank if prepaid, cost one if not) is exact, not asymptotic.

name: treat_m1_interval_as_independent_cyclic_core
statement: FAILS. Treating a one-private-vertex interval as an independent cyclic core would repeat precisely the connector direction which condition (14) of `recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy.md` was designed to absorb. Such a block cannot be charged locally by conditional defect; it must either pass its boundary residuals to an ancestor or be handled by the global triangular activation budget.
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: acyclic defect-poor blocks with all residuals in the boundary and no ancestor payment. The named external condition (14) is in a file the campaign has established does not exist on any machine we control -- see recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy_condition_14.

name: recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy_condition_14
statement: S14 sec.8 names condition (14) of `recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy.md` as the clause designed to ABSORB the connector direction that a one-private-vertex interval would otherwise repeat. That is the identification of the external telescope file's condition (14) with the connector-absorption condition R cap span W contained in R_<. The file itself is cited but NOT reproduced anywhere in the dossier.
notes: The campaign established (2026-08-19, conclusive search) that this file exists on NO machine we control; reconstruction is the only path. Within pp.156-200 this single sentence is the only specification of what condition (14) says.

name: s14_section8_three_phenomena_separation
statement: (S14 sec.8.) Three phenomena separated cleanly. (a) A closed rooted NAE cycle with the homogenizer in the boundary is genuinely cyclic and CONNECTOR-COMPATIBLE: selector rank ceil(n/3), residual space with no boundary intersection, conditional defect paying that rank with coefficient 2. (b) Cutting the cycle to an interval preserves an exact boundary-containing selector basis; every interval with at least two private vertices has a uniform conditional linear bound, and all but the three-vertex one have the stronger activation-cell certificate. (c) A one-private-vertex interval cannot be charged locally by conditional defect; it must pass its boundary residuals to an ancestor or be handled by the global triangular activation budget.
notes: S14's own conclusion from (a)-(c): 'rooted NAE cycles themselves are not an obstruction to the desired connector theorem. Their only boundary pathology occurs after cutting them into an acyclic one-vertex interval, and that pathology is exactly resolved by ancestor residual absorption rather than by a new cyclic estimate.' || READING WARNING: this is a statement about the rooted-NAE family, NOT about the residual class. It says the solved family is compatible with the target; it does not touch dense connector-incoherent cores. The dossier's own words at p.185 remain: 'The remaining global problem is to replace these short-gap witnesses by an entropy-weighted analogue in an arbitrary singleton-layer cyclic block.'

name: L_Q_given_W_conditional_defect_in_S14
statement: The conditional defect used throughout S14: for a private junction basis Q and incoming boundary W, L_{Q|W} = |Q| - H(Q | W) (bits). Cycle instance: L_{Q|W} = n - H(B_1,...,B_n | W) (eq (29)). Interval instance: L_{Q|W} = m - H(B_1,...,B_m | W) with W = {A, B_0, B_{m+1}} (eq (49)).
notes: H is Shannon entropy in bits under the fibre's own (uniform-on-the-fibre) law; conditioning is on the actual boundary VALUES, which is what makes 'target-uniform' a strictly stronger property than a marginal bound.

name: local_rerun_exhaustive_dgeo_minimality
statement: Independent exhaustive check of d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3) for n = 4..8. Search is faithful because any R_0 of dimension w spanned by zero-class forms and signed differences has a w-element basis among those generators, so enumerating all w-subsets for w <= ceil(n/3)-1 covers every candidate. Result (n, d, r, #generators, #candidates, min classes achieved, feasible hits): (4,2,5,69,69,6,0) (5,2,6,107,107,8,0) (6,2,7,152,152,10,0) (7,3,8,205,21100,9,0) (8,3,9,266,35494,11,0). ZERO residual spaces of dimension <= ceil(n/3)-1 achieve the feasibility threshold of r = n+1 signed classes.
source: computed by this digester 2026-08-19; claim under test is dossier p.156 (S10 lines 20-22)
notes: Exact rational arithmetic (fractions.Fraction), exhaustive in the stated finite window n = 4..8 ONLY. This is evidence about a finite range, never a proof of the uniform-in-n theorem, which is S10 (26)-(29). It does independently reproduce S14 (22)'s values 2,2,2,3,3 by a different route than S13's checker.

name: local_rerun_m3_and_m1_falsifiers_fire_exactly_where_predicted

(a) Interval cellwise bound |cell| <= 2^{m-d_m-|z|} on the neutral boundary fibre, using table (41)'s U: m=2 (U={2}, d=1, fibre 3) 0 violations; m=3 (U={1,3}, d=2, fibre 5) EXACTLY 1 violation at z=(1,1), count 1 > 1/2, and the aggregate 5 <= 2^3(3/4)^2 = 4.5 is false; m=4 (fibre 8), m=5 (13), m=6 (21), m=7 (34) all 0 violations. (b) m=1 with k attachments: H(B_1|A,B_0,B_2) = 2^{k+1}/(2^{k+1}+3) and L_{Q|W} = 3/(2^{k+1}+3) reproduced exactly as rationals for k = 0..7 (3/5, 3/7, 3/11, 3/19, 3/35, 3/67, 3/131, 3/259).

name: activation_cell_bound_is_not_tight_on_the_cycle
statement: MEASURED CAVEAT (this digester). The cycle activation-cell inequality |cell| <= 2^{n-|U|-|z|} is not what pins the dimension: on C_12 it holds with ZERO violations for every U tried -- the construction's U (gaps 3,3,3,3), a non-dominating independent U (gaps 4,4,4), a NON-independent U containing an adjacent pair, a U with three consecutive vertices, and oversized independent U's of size 5 and 6. Its aggregate consequence |A_n|/2^{n+1} <= (3/4)^d is loose by a factor 2-5 against the exact Lucas density (n=16: L_n/2^n = 0.0337 vs (3/4)^6 = 0.1780; n=12: 0.0786 vs 0.3164).
source: computed by this digester 2026-08-19; bounds under test are dossier p.178 (S12 (14),(15)) and p.190 (S14 (26))
notes: Consistent with S12's own words that (15) is weaker than the exact Lucas density but 'tensor-stable'. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROGRAMME: an entropy-weighted generalization of the activation profile alone cannot recover a d_geo lower bound; every lower bound in this range comes from the mod-2 two-shadow lemma. My first attempt at this control was mis-designed (shrinking |U| WEAKENS the bound, so it could never fire); the corrected control above is what is reported.

name: coverage_check_enforces_dominating_gaps
statement: MEASURED (this digester). The two halves of the certificate enforce different hypotheses. Running S13's coordinate-basis-and-coverage check on C_12 with various U: construction U = {0,3,6,9} (gaps 3,3,3,3) -> coordinate basis OK, 0 uncovered forms; U = {0,4,8} (gaps 4,4,4, independent but NOT dominating) -> still a coordinate basis but 3 UNCOVERED forms, so no valid certificate at dimension 3; U = {0,1,4,8} (adjacent pair) -> 2 uncovered forms; U = {0,2,4,6,8,10} (all gaps 2, oversized) -> 0 uncovered. So the gaps <= 3 (domination) hypothesis is enforced by SELECTOR COVERAGE, while the activation-cell inequality is indifferent to it.
source: computed by this digester 2026-08-19; construction under test is dossier pp.175-177 (S12 lines 86-142)
notes: This locates precisely which of S12 sec.6's three ingredients each check certifies: ingredient (2) (full-dual coordinate transversal) is the one that fails first when the short-gap structure is broken. A future generalization to arbitrary singleton-layer cyclic blocks must therefore reproduce the TRANSVERSAL, not just the counting profile.
